limitations: These are supporting input locations, not the missing RCIsuit connectivity or dCCI/impact-ranking outputs.
Current and future are source scenario labels. Feature observation dates and commissioning dates are not established.
Several auxiliary field definitions and the relationships among the three dam-status columns remain unresolved.
One Country value is null. Source spelling, capitalization, status labels and nulls are retained.
The authors report checking barriers against imagery and planning documents; that verification was not repeated in this pilot.

source_sheet_annotations.study_objective: The goal of our study was to evaluate the interplay of climate change and barrier-driven river fragmentation on frugivorous fisheries resources across the Amazon basin focused on the accessibility of suitable areas in the years to come.
source_sheet_annotations.study_location: the entire Amazon basin, including regions from Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, and Peru
source_sheet_annotations.dataset_description: Climatic-environmental suitability and presence-absence potential distribution of 52 frugivorous fish species of socioeconomic value, projected on the hydrographic network of the Amazon River basin for both the present and the future under two climatic scenarios (moderate: SSP2-4.5 and pessimistic: SSP5-8.5).
source_sheet_annotations.relationship_description: The distribution of the species was modeled as a function of bioclimatic and hydrological variables (Table S4) covering the Amazon hydrographic network.
source_sheet_annotations.Notes: SR: Yes, spatial asset file for presence/absence of fish of socioeconomic value (current and projectec)

annotations.doi_scope: The dataset DOI identifies the original deposited package. This preparation has no separately registered DOI.
processing: Convert all 562 records from the supplied UTF-8 Shapefile to one GeoPackage layer.
Preserve native WGS84 (EPSG:4326) coordinates, record order, all 31 attributes, nulls, category spelling, current/future labels and per-record source references.
No reprojection, filtering, geometry repair, snapping, status harmonization, connectivity calculation or barrier ranking.
GeoPackage stores numeric values in native SQLite numeric types rather than Shapefile display widths/decimal declarations; decoded values must remain exactly equal.

properties.title: Tropical forest biomass vulnerability (TFVI), 0.1-degree grid
properties.description: Tropical Forest Vulnerability Index for above-ground biomass, supplied with Saatchi et al. (2021). Negative values indicate vulnerability toward sustained biomass loss; positive values indicate vulnerability toward higher biomass. Values near zero indicate relative stability. This is a modeled, standardized index, not a biomass stock map or a probability.

publications.title: Detecting vulnerability of humid tropical forests to multiple stressors
publications.citation: Saatchi, S., et al. (2021). Detecting vulnerability of humid tropical forests to multiple stressors. One Earth 4(7), 988-1003. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oneear.2021.06.002

annotations.preparation_status: Prepared and checked for the EOLab pilot; scientific limitations remain.
limitations: This pilot preserves the published pan-tropical grid; it is not an Amazon-only subset.
The native file contains substantial negative and positive extremes. These must not be clipped, converted to percentages or interpreted as probabilities.
The 0.1-degree source is not the 0.25-degree visualization shown in the main paper. A second 0.1-degree file in FigureS11 is an exact duplicate and should not become a second dataset.
The paper treats the findings as correlational. The model assumes stationary sensitivities and resilience and does not estimate societal impacts.
The paper specifically notes weaker consistency between AGB vulnerability and variance patterns, potentially related to shorter/annual biomass records.
The scientific analysis was not rerun. Format conversion verifies data preservation, not the correctness of the study model.
Exact map observation dates are not embedded. Preserve documented input/study periods separately and label any file-modification temporal fallback.

source_sheet_annotations.study_objective: Here, we develop a tropical forest vulnerability index (TFVI) to detect and evaluate the vulnerability of global tropical forests to threats across space and time.
source_sheet_annotations.study_location: the tropical and subtropical moist forests (HTFs); the study domain for the tropical moist forests is more than 2,000 Mha covering all three continents
source_sheet_annotations.dataset_description: Maps of vulnerability of humid tropical forests derived from the hybrid autoregression model (hybrid AR1) for above-ground biomass; the absolute magnitude of TFVI represents the risk of critical transitions that would result in abrupt decreases or increases of the response variable given long-term trends in the stressors.
source_sheet_annotations.relationship_description: We then used additive regression AR1 models to simultaneously assess the relationship of temporal autocorrelation to multiple stressors.
